subject: Post-call follow-up: ACME model-fit recommendations and streaming coherence
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap — model fit & streaming follow-ups

Hi Jane — thanks again for taking the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary from today's discovery:
- Primary ACME objective: summarize and classify incoming support tickets (short-to-medium length) and generate suggested responses with a 95% precision threshold for intent classification.
- Streaming UX matter: your product team wants partial responses visible in-app for faster agent triage but flagged a couple of cases where partial output cut off mid-sentence or returned duplicate fragments (stop-sequence handling).
- Latency target: 250ms p50 for initial token, 500ms p95 end-to-end for short responses (~60 tokens).

Recommended immediate plan (low-friction eval):
1) Run two model families in parallel across a 2-day eval window with ACME prompt set:
   - Candidate A (higher-quality, heavier): "Redwood-verified-13B-llm-q4f16" (higher-context quality; expect higher cost).
   - Candidate B (fast/cheap): "Redwood-mid-7B-uf8" (optimized for streaming, lower cost).
2) Streaming UX config to test:
   - Enable prefix KV caching and set stop-sequence heuristic to ["

", "# end"] + token-based soft-stop at 3 tokens of low-confidence.
   - Vary chunk sizes: 1-token vs 4-token emission to measure partial coherence vs latency.
3) Evaluation metrics: classification precision/recall, ROUGE-L for generated suggestions, user-visible partial-coherence score (human judgment sample), token-level latency histogram.
4) Security/compliance: we can run the eval in Redwood Dedicated if you prefer isolation; otherwise hosted with SOC2 logging.

Deliverables I'll provide this week:
- prompt_set_acme_v1.csv (attached) 
- a short eval plan + benchmark links (will share a Drive folder)
- cost/latency estimate for a 48-hour soak run and a projected monthly baseline if we roll out production.

Questions for you:
- Can you share a 200‑example sample of real prompts (anonymized) by EOD Wednesday?
- Procurement: is there a PO template or we should route to procurement@acme.com?

Next steps (proposed):
- Jane confirms sample availability and PO path.
- Upon sample receipt, we kick the parallel eval for 48 hours.

Attaching prompt_set_acme_v1.csv and the product spec you shared (acme_service_specs.pdf).

Thanks — looking forward.

Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0199

Attachments: prompt_set_acme_v1.csv (text/csv), acme_service_specs.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — model fit & streaming follow-ups

Sergio — thanks for the thorough recap. A few quick clarifications: 

- We can deliver a 200-example anonymized prompt set by tomorrow afternoon. Good to confirm.
- On stop-sequences: our current frontend strips trailing newlines automatically; part of the partial-token issue might be mismatched client-side trimming. Would you test both with and without client trimming so we can isolate?
- Latency targets: 250ms p50 is ideal but we can accept 400ms p95 during the eval. Can you include a cost delta for the higher-quality 13B candidate?
- Procurement: I'll loop in procurement@acme.com for PO template — cc’d.

Thanks,
Jane
Senior Product Manager, ACME Corporation

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 11:10:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: ACME eval plan + model recommendations (action items)

Team — following Jane's reply, please see recommended internal action items for the 48-hour eval. This email is internal only.

Context: ACME wants classification + generation with streaming partial outputs visible. They reported partial-token duplication and truncation. We need a plan that balances quality vs latency and highlights regression risks related to quantization.

Model recommendations (two arms):
- Arm A (Quality-first): Redwood-verified-13B-llm-q4f16
   - Rationale: best end-to-end generated suggestion quality; expected higher token-cost and longer tail latency.
   - Risk: quantization to q4f16 may introduce occasional decoding artifacts on edge cases — include regression tests.
- Arm B (Streaming-first): Redwood-mid-7B-uf8
   - Rationale: engineered for lower emission latency and stable streaming behavior. Better p50 token latency and cheaper.

Streaming config to A/B test:
- Prefix KV cache: ON (reduces repeated context compute).
- Emission chunk sizes: 1-token and 4-token experiments.
- Stop sequence heuristics: test standard newline + app-level trimming vs soft-stop (confidence threshold).
- Logging: token-level latencies + token confidence scores forwarded to our trace collector.

Evals to run (Rishi):
- Run the ACME prompt_set_acme_v1.csv across both arms for 48 hours in hosted sandbox. Collect: token latency histograms, classification confusion matrices, ROUGE-L, and small human-judgment panel for partial-coherence on 60 samples.
- Add an additional regression suite that feeds adversarial examples (short, punctuated fragments) to detect quantization-induced hallucinations.

Marissa: can you draft a canary rollout plan (A/B 10%/90% with rollback & fallback to Arm B) and a short explainer for the ACME product team on client-side trimming implications?

Priya: please prepare a short pricing delta for a 48-hour soak and a normalized monthly projection for both arms. Include Dedicated vs Hosted numbers if procurement wants isolation.

Attachments: acme_eval_plan.md (attached) — quick checklist and runbook.

I'll share the Drive folder link (internal) with Jane after we confirm they can upload the 200 samples. Deal id is ACME-2026-004.

Thanks — Sergio

Attachments: acme_eval_plan.md (text/markdown)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal: ACME eval plan + model recommendations (action items)

Thanks — I’ll kick off the eval this afternoon. Plan summary: 

- Spin up two sandbox runs (Arm A + Arm B) in hosted infra with token-level tracing enabled.
- Run on the 200-sample set plus 50 adversarial cases. Expect ~6 hours to finish initial pass and produce the automated metrics. Human-judgment panel for partial-coherence will take ~24 hours to schedule; we can ship preliminary numbers before that.
- For streaming tests: will capture emission traces and compute three metrics — token continuity score (detects duplicate fragments), stop-sequence false-positive rate, and p50/p95 token latency.
- If we observe coherence regressions with q4f16, I'll toggle a higher-precision run (q5-like profile) for a small subset to confirm whether artifacts are quantization-driven.

Will update HubSpot deal with a link to the raw metrics once the run completes: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/ACME-2026-004

—Rishi
Applied ML / Evals | Redwood Inference
